units: pixels (image x right, y down) and seconds; no metric scale assumed

camera.motion: static (background difference frame 0 vs 72 in object-free regions: mean 0.36 / 0.53 grey levels; no pan, no shake)
camera.perspective: 2D side view: both objects move horizontally in planes facing the camera; horizon is a straight horizontal line at y=567. Apparent sizes are constant over time (shark length 274+-2 px, boat hull top edge fixed at y=367-368), so a single px scale applies to each object. Whether boat and shark share one depth/scale is unknown (they are separate layers: sea surface above y=673, underwater blue band below).

objects.name: boat
objects.description: red-and-white fishing boat with hull number 'AH805', white wheelhouse, mast, stern railings; floats on the grey sea surface in the upper part of the frame; bow points right
objects.motion: translates to the RIGHT, horizontal only; at rest frames 0-1, then constant 17.88 px/frame (std 0.11) through frame 72
objects.fully_in_frame_x: frames 0-47 (bow reaches the right edge at frame 48); mast top is cut by the top image edge in every frame where the mast is visible (mast leaves frame at frame 68-69)
objects.reference_point: ref_x = 657.5 (midpoint of stern 228 and bow 1087 at frame 0) + measured shift of the stern rail post; ref_y = 488 (midpoint of hull top at bow y=367 and visible keel y~610). The true Blender origin is not visible; since motion is pure horizontal translation, any rigid point gives the same displacement.

extents_frame0_px.overall_length_note: stern x=228 (mask, incl. soft edge; stern hull edge at 50% contrast x=237) to bow tip x=1087
extents_frame0_px.mast_top_y: <=0 (cut by top edge); mast x ~705-722, centre 711.9
extents_frame0_px.visible_height_from_top_edge_to_keel: ~610 (lower bound of true height; mast truncated)

objects.name: shark
objects.description: grey shark (white belly, dorsal fin) swimming underwater in the blue band in the lower part of the frame; nose points left
objects.motion: translates to the LEFT, horizontal only (centroid y 905.4+-0.2); at rest frames 0-1, then constant 10.76 px/frame (std ~0.08) through frame 72
objects.fully_in_frame: frames 0-63; nose touches the left image edge from frame 64 (cut afterwards)
objects.reference_point: ref_x/ref_y = bbox centre at frame 0 (810.5, 904.0) + sub-pixel template shift of the shark's body

objects.name: horizon / sea surface
objects.description: sky (grey gradient) meets the sea at y=567 (straight, horizontal across the full width); sea surface band y=567-673

objects.name: underwater blue band
objects.description: flat blue region from y=674 to the bottom edge (y=1079), where the shark swims

events.event: both boat and shark at rest (frames 0 and 1 identical)
motion starts: boat moves right, shark moves left (first displacement between frame 1 and 2)
boat bow reaches right image edge (bow x=1910 at frame 47)
shark nose reaches left image edge (nose x=8 at frame 63)
boat mast (centre x=711.9+17.88*(f-1)) reaches the right edge at frame 68 and is gone at frame 69; rigging lines leave by frame 70 (bbox top jumps from 0 to 231)
clip ends, both still moving at constant pixel speed
